primary_question: Why does my aloo paratha keep tearing?
seo_title: Why does my aloo paratha keep tearing? | SattvaSrsti
meta_description: Learn why your aloo paratha keeps tearing and how to fix it with these helpful tips.

humanized.hook: Struggling with tearing aloo parathas? You're not alone!
story: Making aloo parathas can be a comforting start to your day, but when they tear, it can be frustrating.
The key to perfecting this dish lies in the details of your dough and filling.
humanized.useful_answer: If your aloo paratha is tearing, it might be due to overboiling the potatoes, making them mushy. Aim for a soft texture without lumps, and ensure your dough isn't too sticky. Also, avoid pressing too hard while rolling to keep the edges sealed.

common_questions.q: Why does my aloo paratha keep tearing?
common_questions.a: Usually the dough is too sticky or you are pressing too hard while rolling — keep the dough soft and smooth, seal the edges, then roll gently for even thickness. That small change has saved more Sunday breakfasts than any new recipe ever did.

common_questions.q: Why does the stuffing come out while rolling?
common_questions.a: The filling spilled past the seal or was a bit wet — keep it centered and pinch the edges closed before you roll. Once the seal holds, the paratha finally behaves.

common_questions.q: Why is my potato filling lumpy?
common_questions.a: Lumps left in the mash poke through the dough — mash until the mixture is uniform before you stuff. Smooth filling is half the battle won.

common_questions.q: How do I know the dough is ready?
common_questions.a: It should feel smooth, not sticky on your fingers — if it clings, it is too wet. Trust that soft, even feel before you start rolling.

common_questions.q: What should I serve with aloo paratha?
common_questions.a: Yogurt, pickle, and butter are the classic trio with this breakfast. Keep the sides simple and let the hot paratha do the talking.

humanized.emotional_ending: With a bit of attention to detail, your aloo parathas can turn out perfectly every time.
